title: 逛街買鞋與大小
subtitle: Buying clothes and shoes, and describing size and degree

example.hanzi: 這雙鞋很漂亮，我想試穿。
example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié hěn piàoliàng, wǒ xiǎng shì chuān.
example.gloss: This pair of shoes is pretty; I'd like to try them on.

example.hanzi: 我買了兩雙鞋，一雙黑的，一雙白的。
example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng shuāng xié, yì shuāng hēi de, yì shuāng bái de.
example.gloss: I bought two pairs of shoes, one black pair and one white pair.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfú tài duǎn le, wǒ bú tài xǐhuān.
example.gloss: This piece of clothing is too short; I don't really like it.

example.hanzi: 老闆，請幫我把鞋包起來。
example.pinyin: Lǎobǎn, qǐng bāng wǒ bǎ xié bāo qǐlái.
example.gloss: Boss, please wrap the shoes up for me.

example.hanzi: 我的鞋壞了，要買一雙新的。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de xié huài le, yào mǎi yì shuāng xīn de.
example.gloss: My shoes are broken; I need to buy a new pair.

grammar.title: The measure word 雙 for things that come in pairs
grammar.pattern: Number + 雙 + Noun（鞋／腳／手／眼睛）
grammar.explanation: 雙 is the measure word for things that naturally come in twos: shoes, feet, hands, eyes, chopsticks. Say 一雙鞋 (one pair of shoes), 兩雙鞋 (two pairs). You can also drop the noun when it is clear: 我要這雙 ('I want this pair'). With 這／那, no number is needed: 這雙鞋.
grammar.contrast: 件 vs 雙: 件 counts single garments (一件衣服), 雙 counts paired items (一雙鞋). Ask yourself whether the thing is normally used two-at-a-time; if yes, use 雙.
grammar.common_error: Learners say 一個鞋 or 一件鞋. 個 is the all-purpose measure word, but for shoes Taiwanese speakers always say 一雙鞋. Also remember 雙 already means the pair, so 兩雙鞋 is four shoes, not two.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào mǎi yì shuāng yùndòng xié.
examples.gloss: I want to buy a pair of sports shoes.

examples.hanzi: 這兩雙鞋都不錯，我很難選。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng shuāng xié dōu búcuò, wǒ hěn nán xuǎn.
examples.gloss: Both pairs of shoes are nice; it's hard for me to choose.

examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu yì shuāng hěn dà de yǎnjīng.
examples.gloss: She has a pair of big eyes.

passage.title: 買鞋
passage.hanzi: 週末我跟妹妹去買東西。我的鞋壞了，所以想買一雙新的。店裡的鞋很多，我試穿了一雙黑色的，可是有一點短，老闆就幫我換了大一號的。這雙很舒服，也不貴，我很喜歡。老闆把鞋包好，還說下次再來。
passage.gloss: On the weekend I went shopping with my younger sister. My shoes were broken, so I wanted to buy a new pair. The shop had lots of shoes. I tried on a black pair, but they were a bit short, so the owner changed them for a size bigger. This pair was comfortable and not expensive — I really liked them. The owner wrapped the shoes up and said to come again next time.

example.hanzi: 他的中文極好,幾乎跟台灣人一樣。
example.pinyin: Tā de Zhōngwén jí hǎo, jīhū gēn Táiwān rén yíyàng.
example.gloss: His Chinese is extremely good, almost like a Taiwanese person's.

example.hanzi: 我幾乎每天都騎腳踏車上班。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jīhū měi tiān dōu qí jiǎotàchē shàngbān.
example.gloss: I ride my bike to work almost every day.

vocab.gloss: different; wrong; mistaken; to fall short; to lack

example.hanzi: 這家店的服務很差,我不想再來了。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de fúwù hěn chà, wǒ bù xiǎng zài lái le.
example.gloss: The service at this shop is bad; I don't want to come again.

example.hanzi: 這裡的房租比較低,所以我住這邊。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fángzū bǐjiào dī, suǒyǐ wǒ zhù zhè biān.
example.gloss: The rent here is fairly low, so I live on this side of town.

example.hanzi: 我們八點半在捷運站見,好嗎?
example.pinyin: Wǒmen bā diǎn bàn zài jiéyùn zhàn jiàn, hǎo ma?
example.gloss: Let's meet at the MRT station at eight thirty, OK?

example.pinyin: Tā de Zhōngwén shuǐpíng hěn gāo o.
example.gloss: His Chinese level is really high.

grammar.title: 用「幾乎」說「差一點就…」
grammar.pattern: Subject + 幾乎 + (都 / 沒) + Verb / Adjective
grammar.explanation: 「幾乎」means "almost, nearly" and always goes BEFORE the verb or adjective, never after it. With a positive verb it often takes 都 (幾乎都…) to mean "almost all / almost every time"; with a negative it means "nearly didn't happen at all" (幾乎沒…、幾乎不…). It describes how close something is to being complete, so it works well when you talk about level: 我的水平幾乎跟他一樣高。
grammar.contrast: 「差不多」also means "about / almost", but it is more relaxed and can stand alone as a whole answer (好了嗎?差不多了。). 「幾乎」cannot stand alone — it must sit in front of a verb or adjective. Use 差不多 for a rough estimate (差不多三點), and 幾乎 when you want to stress that only a tiny bit is missing (幾乎三點了 sounds wrong; 幾乎沒錢了 is right).
grammar.common_error: Learners copy English word order and put 幾乎 at the end, e.g. saying 「我懂幾乎」or 「我的水平高幾乎」. It must come before what it modifies: 我幾乎都懂、我的水平幾乎一樣高。

examples.hanzi: 我幾乎每天都喝一杯咖啡。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīhū měi tiān dōu hē yì bēi kāfēi.
examples.gloss: I drink a cup of coffee almost every day.

examples.hanzi: 他跑得太快,我幾乎跟不上。
examples.pinyin: Tā pǎo de tài kuài, wǒ jīhū gēn bú shàng.
examples.gloss: He runs too fast; I almost can't keep up.

examples.hanzi: 這兩件衣服的顏色差不多,不過這件比較貴。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiàn yīfú de yánsè chàbùduō, búguò zhè jiàn bǐjiào guì.
examples.gloss: These two shirts are about the same colour, but this one is more expensive.

dialogue.speaker: 大明
dialogue.pinyin: Bié wèn le la, wǒ kǎo de hěn chà.
dialogue.gloss: Don't even ask — I did really badly.

dialogue.hanzi: 真的嗎?你的中文水平不低啊。
dialogue.pinyin: Zhēn de ma? Nǐ de Zhōngwén shuǐpíng bù dī a.
dialogue.gloss: Really? Your Chinese level isn't low at all.

dialogue.hanzi: 那個考試太難了,我幾乎都不懂。

dialogue.gloss: That test was too hard; I almost didn't understand any of it.

dialogue.hanzi: 別擔心,下次一定會更好,你進步極快。
dialogue.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, xià cì yídìng huì gèng hǎo, nǐ jìnbù jí kuài.
dialogue.gloss: Don't worry, next time will definitely be better — you're improving extremely fast.

dialogue.gloss: I hope so! I still have class at three thirty.

sentences.gloss: His Chinese level is very high.

sentences.gloss: The rent in this area is relatively low.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒmen qī diǎn bàn zài chēzhàn jiàn.
sentences.gloss: We'll meet at the station at seven thirty.

passage.title: 我的游泳水平
passage.hanzi: 以前我的游泳水平很低,幾乎不會游。從去年開始,我每個週末都去學校附近的運動中心游泳。那裡的水溫比較低,一開始我真的很不習慣,學得也很差。老師常說:慢慢來就好。現在我一次能游半個小時,他說我的水平進步極快。
passage.gloss: My swimming used to be at a very low level — I could hardly swim at all. Starting last year, I went swimming every weekend at the sports centre near my school. The water there is fairly cold, and at first I really wasn't used to it and learned very poorly. My teacher often said: just take it slowly. Now I can swim for half an hour at a time, and he says my level has improved extremely fast.
